docstring:
The element of invariant `p / n` generates a group carrying an invariant map onto the
`n`-torsion.
description: **Generator of a torsion-isomorphic group.** Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a linearly ordered field with $p > 0$, let $n$ be a positive natural number, and let $H$ be an additive group. Suppose $f : H \to \mathbb{R}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is an injective group homomorphism whose image is exactly the subgroup of $n$-torsion elements of the circle $\mathbb{R}/p\mathbb{Z}$. If $u \in H$ satisfies $f(u) = [p/n]$, the class of $p/n$ in the circle, then every element $x \in H$ is an integer multiple of $u$. In other words, $H$ is cyclic and generated by $u$.

name: TauCeti.AlbertAlgebra

docstring:
The **split Albert algebra** `H₃(𝕆)` over `R`: a `3 × 3` Hermitian matrix over the split
octonions, recorded as its scalar diagonal together with its three octonion entries.
description: **Split Albert algebra.** For a commutative ring $R$, the split Albert algebra $H_3(\mathbb{O})$ over $R$ is the algebra of $3 \times 3$ Hermitian matrices with entries in the split octonions over $R$. An element is specified by its three diagonal entries, which are scalars in $R$, together with three off-diagonal octonion entries, each taken from the split octonions over $R$.

name: TauCeti.AlbertAlgebra.neg_diag

description: **Negation commutes with taking the diagonal.** For any type $R$ with a negation operation and any element $A$ of the Albert algebra over $R$, the diagonal of $-A$ equals the negative of the diagonal of $A$. Here the diagonal of an Albert algebra element is its triple of diagonal entries, so the identity says that negating $A$ and then reading off its diagonal gives the same result as reading off the diagonal of $A$ and negating each of the three entries.

Over commutative rings, `gaPointsMulEquiv` identifies the convolution inverse of a
`𝔾ₐ`-point with negation in the value ring.
description: **Convolution inverse corresponds to negation.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra. A $\mathbb{G}_a$-point is an $R$-algebra homomorphism from the symmetric algebra of $R$ over $R$ to $A$, and these form a group under the convolution product. For any such point $F$, the image of its convolution inverse $F^{-1}$ under the identification $\mathrm{gaPointsMulEquiv}$ equals the inverse (in the target group, which is the additive group of the value ring $A$) of the image of $F$. In other words, the identification sends convolution inverses to additive negatives in $A$.

map from `R[N]` to the group algebra of the character cokernel.

The Hopf ideal defining its kernel (viewed as a Hopf-algebra kernel, then extracted as an ordinary ideal) coincides with the ordinary kernel of the ring homomorphism $R[N] \to R[N/p(M)]$ that sends each group element $n \in N$ to its coset $n\,p(M)$ in the quotient group $N/p(M)$.

Maps from the fppf quotient sheaf to a group object in fppf sheaves are naturally equivalent

Let $F$ be a group object in the category of fppf sheaves of sets (on commutative $R$-algebras). In other words, the determinant of the represented weight torus is one exactly when the weights sum to zero.

The quotient coordinate morphism from `O(GL (m + m))` to the symplectic coordinate Hopf

description: **Coordinate map for the symplectic group.** For a commutative ring $R$ and a natural number $m$, this is the quotient morphism from the coordinate Hopf algebra of the general linear group $GL_{2m}(R)$ to the coordinate Hopf algebra of the symplectic group $Sp_{2m}(R)$ (viewed as the orthogonal-type quotient $\mathcal{O}(GL_{m+m})$ in the docstring's notation). Consider the convolution-type group structure on $R$-algebra endomorphisms $R \to A$ (the $R$-algebra homomorphisms from $R$ to $A$, viewed in the convolution structure via the `WithConv` wrapper). For any such homomorphism $f$ and any element $r \in R$, applying the inverse of $f$ to $r$ yields the same result as applying the structure map $\mathrm{algebraMap}: R \to A$ to $r$; that is, $(f^{-1})(r) = \mathrm{algebraMap}_R^A(r)$.

name: TauCeti.Bigraded.eulerMonoidHom
signature: def TauCeti.Bigraded.eulerMonoidHom : Multiplicative (ℤ × ℤ) →* LaurentPolynomial ℤ
docstring:
The Alexander-graded Euler characteristic of a bigraded vector space, as a monoid
homomorphism on bidegrees: bidegree `(m, a)` contributes `(-1)^m T^a`.
description: **Alexander-graded Euler characteristic.** The Euler characteristic map is a monoid homomorphism from the group of bidegrees $(m, a) \in \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$ (regarded as a multiplicative monoid, so the operation is addition of bidegrees) into the ring of Laurent polynomials in a variable $T$ with integer coefficients. It sends each bidegree $(m, a)$ to the monomial $(-1)^m T^a$, so that the images of products of bidegrees are products of the corresponding Laurent monomials, with the identity bidegree $(0,0)$ going to $1$.

An equivalence of module categories pulls the finitely generated projective `B`-modules back
to the finitely generated projective `A`-modules.

Then the class of finitely generated projective $A$-modules is exactly the preimage of the class of finitely generated projective $B$-modules under the functor $e$ (equivalently, an $A$-module $M$ is finitely generated projective if and only if $e(M)$ is a finitely generated projective $B$-module).

name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_biprod

If $M$ and $N$ are sheaves of $R$-modules that are each of finite type, then their direct sum (biproduct) $M \oplus N$ is also a sheaf of $R$-modules of finite type.

Restriction after sheafification is naturally isomorphic to sheafification after restriction
of presheaves.

Then there is a natural isomorphism between two functors from presheaves of $R$-modules to sheaves of modules over the restricted ring sheaf $R|_{X}$ on the slice: the first applies sheafification of $R$-modules and then restricts to $X$; the second restricts to $X$ first, then pushes forward along the ring isomorphism identifying $R|_{X}$ (viewed on the slice over $X$ via the forgetful functor) with the restricted ring sheaf, and finally sheafifies. description: **Internal Decomposition Restricted to a Component-Stable Submodule.** Let $V$ be an $S$-module that is the internal direct sum of a family of submodules $(A_i)_{i\in\kappa}$, so every element of $V$ decomposes uniquely as a finite sum of components taken from the $A_i$. The bigraded `Ext` groups of `(X, Y)` **assemble into the ungraded `Ext` groups** of a pair
`(X', Y')`: in every cohomological degree the direct sum over the internal degrees of
`Ext^n(X, Y{j})` is `Ext^n(X', Y')`.

This is the hypothesis under which a q-Euler form specializes at `q = 1` to an ordinary Ext-Euler
characteristic.  A functor forgetting the grading supplies the intended pairs `(U X, U Y)`; the
existence of such a functor, or even of a shift-compatible one, does not by itself supply these
isomorphisms.

The statement asserts that the bigraded Ext groups of $(X, Y)$ assemble into the ungraded Ext groups of $(X', Y')$: for every cohomological degree $n$, the direct sum over internal degrees $j$ of $\operatorname{Ext}^n(X, \sigma^j Y)$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Ext}^n(X', Y')$. This is an extra hypothesis that is not automatic from the existence of a forgetful functor.

A vector `v` of a `gl n R`-module is a **highest weight vector of weight `μ`** for the matrix
unit positive system when it is nonzero, the diagonal matrix unit `Eᵢᵢ` acts on it by the scalar
`μ i`, and every raising matrix unit `Eᵢⱼ` with `i < j` annihilates it.

The two elementwise families are coordinates for the diagonal Cartan subalgebra and generators of
the positive nilpotent subalgebra `𝔫⁺` — the nilpotent ideal of the standard Borel subalgebra
`TauCeti.upperTriangular R n`, not an ideal of `gl n R` — so this says exactly that `v` is a
`𝔫⁺`-annihilated weight
vector of weight `TauCeti.glWeightEquiv R n μ`; see
`TauCeti.isGlHighestWeightVector_iff_forall_mem`.
description: **Highest weight vector for $\mathfrak{gl}_n(R)$.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $n$ a finite linearly ordered index set, and $M$ an $R$-module carrying a Lie module structure over the matrix Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_n(R)$. For a weight $\mu : n \to R$ and a vector $v \in M$, the statement says that $v$ is a highest weight vector of weight $\mu$ with respect to the matrix unit positive system. This means that $v \neq 0$, that each diagonal matrix unit $E_{ii}$ acts on $v$ as multiplication by $\mu(i)$, and that every raising matrix unit $E_{ij}$ with $i < j$ annihilates $v$.

docstring:
**The bracket of the Heisenberg Lie algebra is a multiple of its central generator.** The
coefficient is the `2 × 2` determinant of the two superdiagonal entries, so the whole bracket
structure of the strict upper triangle in size three is one `2 × 2` determinant.
description:
**Bracket in the Heisenberg Lie algebra.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $\mathfrak{h}$ be the Heisenberg Lie algebra over $R$, realized as the strictly upper triangular $3\times 3$ matrices with the commutator bracket. For any two elements $A, B \in \mathfrak{h}$, the bracket $[A,B]$ is a scalar multiple of the central generator $Z$. Specifically,
$$[A,B] = \left(A_{01}B_{12} - B_{01}A_{12}\right) Z,$$
where $A_{01}, A_{12}$ and $B_{01}, B_{12}$ are the superdiagonal entries of $A$ and $B$. The coefficient is therefore the $2\times 2$ determinant formed from the two superdiagonal entries of $A$ and $B$.

      ⁅TauCeti.serreE R CM i, TauCeti.serreE R CM j⁆ =

docstring: The higher Serre relation on the `E`'s: `(ad Eᵢ) ^ (-CMᵢⱼ).toNat ⁅Eᵢ, Eⱼ⁆ = 0`.
description:
**Higher Serre relation for the generators $E_i$.** Let $B$ be a finite-or-arbitrary index set with decidable equality, let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $CM = (CM_{ij})$ be an integer matrix (a generalized Cartan matrix in the Kac–Moody setting). Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be the Lie algebra over $R$ associated to $CM$, with Chevalley-type generators $E_i$ for $i \in B$. Then for all indices $i, j \in B$, applying the adjoint representation of $E_i$ to the power $(-CM_{ij})^+ = \max(-CM_{ij}, 0)$ times, and then evaluating on the Lie bracket $[E_i, E_j]$, gives zero:
$$\operatorname{ad}(E_i)^{\,-CM_{ij}}\big([E_i, E_j]\big) = 0,$$
where the exponent is taken to be the nonnegative integer $-CM_{ij}$ (and is zero when $CM_{ij} \ge 0$). In other words, $\operatorname{ad}(E_i)^{1-a_{ij}}(E_j) = 0$ type relations hold in the form stated, with the exponent being the truncation of $-CM_{ij}$ to a natural number.

to the ladder operators.

**A monomial-basis numbered symmetry carries the represented weight torus of a weight family
to the weight torus of the relabelled family.** The scalar coefficients do not affect diagonal
conjugation. Stability of a closed subgroup scheme cut out by the root subgroups and a weight torus
additionally requires identifying this relabelled family with the original one, via weight
equivariance and
`GeneralLinear.weightTorusCoordinateMap_reindex`.
description: **Numbered symmetry intertwines weight torus coordinates.** Let $V$ be a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space, $M \subseteq V$ an additive subgroup with a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis $(b_i)_{i \in \{1,\dots,n\}}$, and $\theta$ a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear automorphism of $V$ that preserves $M$ (so $\theta(v) \in M$ exactly when $v \in M$). Let $\iota$ be a finite index type, and let $\mathrm{wt}_i : \iota \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a family of integer weight vectors indexed by $i$. Suppose $\sigma$ is a permutation of the indices and $c_i \in \mathbb{Z}$ are integer scalars such that $\theta(b_i) = c_i \, b_{\sigma(i)}$ for every $i$. Then, composing the coordinate isomorphism induced by $\theta$ on $M$ (the Kostant-numbered symmetry isomorphism) with the weight torus coordinate map for the family $\mathrm{wt}$ gives the same result as applying the weight torus coordinate map to the reindexed family $i \mapsto \mathrm{wt}_{\sigma^{-1}(i)}$. In other words, the nonzero integer scalars $c_i$ play no role, and the symmetry simply relabels the weight family by $\sigma^{-1}$.

entrywise sends the representative over the source ring to the representative over the target

compatibility and the fact that the root vectors and Cartan subalgebra span the ambient Lie
algebra.
description: **Chevalley system relative to a Chevalley involution.** Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Killing Lie algebra over a field $K$, with a Cartan subalgebra $H$ whose action on $L$ is triangularizable. Given a Lie algebra automorphism $\omega$ of $L$ and an assignment sending each root $\alpha$ (a weight of $H$ acting on $L$) to a vector $e_\alpha \in L$, the statement says that this family is a normalized family of root vectors compatible with $\omega$. Each $e_\alpha$ is a root vector, and $\omega$ exchanges $e_\alpha$ with the negative of the root vector for the opposite root, so that $\omega(e_\alpha) = -e_{-\alpha}$, with the normalization conditions also holding. No involutivity of $\omega$ is assumed separately, since it follows from this compatibility together with the fact that the root vectors and $H$ span $L$.

theorem LinearEquiv.map_range_of_intertwine : ∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid N]

docstring:
If a linear equivalence `e` intertwines two endomorphisms `f` and `g` pointwise
(`g (e d) = e (f d)`), it carries the range of `f` onto the range of `g`.
description: **Linear equivalences preserve ranges of intertwined endomorphisms.** Let $R$ be a semiring, let $M$ and $N$ be $R$-modules, and let $e : M \to N$ be a linear isomorphism. Let $f : M \to M$ and $g : N \to N$ be linear maps such that $g(e(d)) = e(f(d))$ for every $d \in M$, i.e., $g \circ e = e \circ f$. Then the image of the range of $f$ under $e$ equals the range of $g$; that is, $e(\operatorname{range} f) = \operatorname{range} g$ as submodules of $N$.

def QuaternionAlgebra.normFormIsometryEquivWeightedSumSquares : {R : Type u_1} →

The coordinates `1, i, j, k` are an isometry from the norm form of `ℍ[R,a,b]` to the diagonal
form `⟨1, -a, -b, ab⟩`, the two-fold Pfister form `⟨⟨a,b⟩⟩`.
description: **Norm form of the quaternion algebra as a weighted sum of squares.** For a commutative ring $R$ and elements $a, b \in R$, the norm form of the quaternion algebra $\mathbb{H}[R,a,b]$ (with its standard basis $1, i, j, k$, where $i^2 = a$, $j^2 = b$, $k = ij$) is isometrically equivalent to the diagonal quadratic form $\langle 1, -a, -b, ab\rangle$, i.e. $x_0^2 - a x_1^2 - b x_2^2 + ab\, x_3^2$. The isometry is given by the coordinate map sending $x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$ to $(x_0, x_1, x_2, x_3)$. This diagonal form is the two-fold Pfister form $\langle\langle a, b\rangle\rangle$.

theorem AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.skyscraperResidueFieldEquiv_map : ∀ {X : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme} (x : ↥X) {U V : X.Opens} (i : U ⟶ V) (hx : x ∈ U)

docstring: The identifications of the sections of `κ(x)ₓ` with `κ(x)` commute with restriction.
description: **Compatibility of the residue field identification with restriction.** Let $X$ be a scheme, $x$ a point of $X$, and let $U \subseteq V$ be open subsets of $X$ with $x \in U$ (the inclusion $U \to V$ being the morphism $i$ in the poset of opens; note $x\in U$ implies $x\in V$). description: **Inverse of the weight-one degree isomorphism.** Let $S$ be an order system on $X$ with values in an abelian group $G$, let $w : X \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a weighting that is weighted-degree-zero for $S$, and let $x_0 \in X$ be a point with $w(x_0) = 1$. In other words, the inverse of the isomorphism sends $n$ to the class of $S.\text{degreeSection}(x_0)(n)$.

name: TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.OrderSystem.equivalence_linearlyEquivalent

theorem TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.OrderSystem.equivalence_linearlyEquivalent : ∀ {X : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} [inst : AddCommGroup G] (S : TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.WeilDivisor.OrderSystem X G),

theorem PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.ElementaryCollapsesTo.map : ∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq β] {K L : PreAbstractSimplicialComplex α},

An injective relabeling preserves an elementary collapse. The deleted free pair is sent to
its image pair.
description: **Image of an elementary collapse under an injective relabeling.** Let $K$ and $L$ be pre-abstract simplicial complexes on a vertex set $\alpha$, where $L$ is obtained from $K$ by an elementary collapse. Let $f:\alpha\to\beta$ be an injective map of vertex sets (with $\beta$ having decidable equality). Then the relabelled complex $K$ mapped along $f$ elementary-collapses to the relabelled complex $L$ mapped along $f$. In other words, the operation of pushing a complex forward along an injective vertex relabeling preserves elementary collapses, and the free pair removed in the collapse is carried to its image pair under $f$.

name: SSet.mayerVietorisToBiprod_fromBiprod_assoc
signature:
theorem SSet.mayerVietorisToBiprod_fromBiprod_assoc : ∀ {C : Type u} [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [inst_1 : CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoproducts C]
  [inst_2 : CategoryTheory.Abelian C] (R : C) {X₁ X₂ X₃ X₄ : SSet} {t : X₁ ⟶ X₂} {l : X₁ ⟶ X₃} {r : X₂ ⟶ X₄}
  {b : X₃ ⟶ X₄},
  CategoryTheory.CommSq t l r b →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) {Z : C} (h : X₄.homology R n ⟶ Z),
      CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (SSet.mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l n)
          (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (SSet.mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b n) h) =
        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp 0 h
description:
**Vanishing of consecutive Mayer–Vietoris maps.** Let $R$ be an object of an abelian category with coproducts, and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc} X_1 & \xrightarrow{\ t\ } & X_2 \\ {\scriptstyle l}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle r} \\ X_3 & \xrightarrow{\ b\ } & X_4 \end{array}$$
be a commutative square of simplicial sets. For every natural number $n$ and every morphism $h\colon H_n(X_4;R)\to Z$, composing the Mayer–Vietoris map $H_n(X_1;R)\to H_n(X_2;R)\oplus H_n(X_3;R)$ with the Mayer–Vietoris map $H_n(X_2;R)\oplus H_n(X_3;R)\to H_n(X_4;R)$ and then with $h$ gives the zero morphism. In other words, two consecutive maps in the Mayer–Vietoris sequence compose to zero, so any further map applied to $H_n(X_4;R)$ kills their composite.

theorem TauCeti.AffineChain.subdivision_single : ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : Convexity.ConvexSpace ℝ E] {k : ℕ} (v : Fin (k + 1) → E) (a : ℤ),

Its subdivision equals the signed sum, over all permutations $\pi$ of $\{0, \dots, k\}$, of the affine simplices obtained by composing the affine map from the standard simplex to $E$ that sends its vertices to $v_0, \dots, v_k$ with the barycentric subdivision simplex indexed by $\pi$. Each such term carries coefficient $a \cdot \operatorname{sign}(\pi)$.

orbit. This uses the orientation of `MulAction.orbitRel_apply`: the left point is a member of
the orbit of the right point.

theorem TauCeti.isOpen_image_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (a e : ι → ℝ) (z₀ : UpperHalfPlane) {s : Set ℂ},

docstring:
**The Schwarz--Christoffel primitive is an open map on the upper half-plane.**  Its derivative
is the integrand, which never vanishes there, so the inverse function theorem makes the image of
every neighbourhood a neighbourhood.
description: **Schwarz–Christoffel primitive is open on the upper half-plane.** Let $\iota$ be a finite index set, and let $a = (a_i)_{i\in\iota}$ and $e = (e_i)_{i\in\iota}$ be families of real numbers. Fix a base point $z_0$ in the upper half-plane. Then for every open subset $s$ of the complex plane that is contained in the upper half-plane, the image of $s$ under the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive (the map defined from these data and the base point $z_0$) is again open in $\mathbb{C}$. In other words, the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive is an open map when restricted to the upper half-plane. This follows because its derivative, the Schwarz–Christoffel integrand, never vanishes there, so the map is locally invertible by the inverse function theorem.

name: TauCeti.pseudoHyperbolicExpr_map_le_unitDisc

docstring: Bundled unit-disc form of the Schwarz--Pick contraction estimate.
description:
**Schwarz–Pick contraction for the unit disc.** Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a function that is complex differentiable on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: |z|<1\}$ and maps $\mathbb{D}$ into itself. Then for all $z,w\in\mathbb{D}$, the pseudo-hyperbolic distance between $f(z)$ and $f(w)$ is at most the pseudo-hyperbolic distance between $z$ and $w$, namely
$$\left|\frac{f(z)-f(w)}{1-\overline{f(w)}\,f(z)}\right| \le \left|\frac{z-w}{1-\overline{w}\,z}\right|,$$
where the pseudo-hyperbolic expression is understood in the standard sense for points of the unit disc.

precompose each defining inequality with the map.
description: **Preimage of a Convex Polyhedron under an Affine Map.** Let $E$ and $F$ be real topological vector spaces, let $u \subseteq F$ be a convex polyhedron, and let $A : E \to F$ be a continuous affine map. Then the preimage $A^{-1}(u) = \{x \in E : A(x) \in u\}$ is a convex polyhedron in $E$. This is proved by composing each of the defining linear inequalities of $u$ with $A$, which yields finitely many defining inequalities for $A^{-1}(u)$.

name: TauCeti.levelSetChartModel_source

theorem TauCeti.levelSetChartModel_source : ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E]

description: **Source of the Level-Set Model Chart.** Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a nontrivially normed, complete field, let $E$ and $F$ be complete normed spaces over $\mathbb{K}$, and let $f : E \to F$ be a function that is strictly differentiable at a point $a \in E$ with derivative $f' : E \to_L F$. Then the source (domain) of the model chart for the level set $\{f = c\}$ constructed from these data coincides with the source of the level-set chart itself. In other words, the model chart and the level-set chart are defined on the same open set.

description:
**Upper tail of the second Euler beta integral.** Let $a, b, u_0$ be real numbers with $0 \le u_0 < 1$. Then

$$\int_{u_0/(1-u_0)}^{\infty} w^{a-1}(1+w)^{-(a+b)}\,dw \;=\; \int_{u_0}^{1} u^{a-1}(1-u)^{b-1}\,du.$$

In words, the integral of $w^{a-1}(1+w)^{-(a+b)}$ over the interval $(u_0/(1-u_0), \infty)$ equals the integral of $u^{a-1}(1-u)^{b-1}$ over the interval $(u_0, 1)$. The identity comes from the substitution $u = w/(1+w)$, which maps $(u_0/(1-u_0), \infty)$ onto $(u_0, 1)$.

name: TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField
signature: structure TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField : (k : Type u_3) → (F : Type u_4) → [inst : Field k] → [inst_1 : Field F] → [Algebra k F] → Prop
docstring:
A **hyperelliptic function field** (Stichtenoth, Definition 6.2.1, with separability of the
index-two subextension made part of the definition): genus at least two together with an element
`x` transcendental over `k` such that `F / k(x)` is separable of degree two.

Being an algebraic function field is *not* part of the predicate: the hypothesis
`TauCeti.IsFunctionField`, like the exactness of the constant field, is kept as a separate
hypothesis on the statements that need it, as everywhere in this development.

In characteristic two an index-two subextension can be purely inseparable, and such an `F` is
deliberately outside this model class; away from characteristic two the separability clause is
automatic, so there the predicate agrees with Stichtenoth's index-two definition.
description:
**Hyperelliptic function field.** Let $k$ be a field and $F$ an extension field of $k$. We say $F$ is a hyperelliptic function field over $k$ when the following two conditions hold:

1. The genus of $F$ is at least two.
2. There exists an element $x \in F$, transcendental over $k$, such that $F$ is a separable extension of the rational function field $k(x)$ of degree two.

Here the separability requirement is part of the definition, so that in characteristic two a purely inseparable quadratic subextension $F/k(x)$ does not qualify. Away from characteristic two, the separability condition holds automatically, and the notion coincides with the usual definition of a hyperelliptic function field (an index-two subextension of $F/k(x)$ of genus at least two). Note that this predicate does not itself require $F$ to be an algebraic function field over $k$, nor that $k$ be the exact constant field; such hypotheses are imposed separately wherever they are needed.

**The rational places of `k(x)` are `ℙ¹(k) = k ∪ {∞}`** (Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.2.3): a
place of `k(x)` has degree one exactly when it is the place at infinity or the place of a linear
polynomial `X - a`.
description: **Rational places of degree one.** For any field $k$, there is a bijection between $k \cup \{\infty\}$ (the projective line $\mathbb{P}^1(k)$ over $k$) and the set of places of the rational function field $k(x)$ having degree one. Under this correspondence, each element $a \in k$ is sent to the place associated with the linear polynomial $x - a$, and the extra element $\infty$ is sent to the place at infinity.

field.
description: **Stabilizer of a root as a point of the root set.** Let $F$ be a field, $M$ a field extension of $F$, and $q$ a polynomial over $F$. Let $\alpha \in M$ be a root of $q$ in $M$, so that $\alpha$ lies in the root set of $q$ in $M$. Then the stabilizer of $\alpha$, viewed as an element of the root set, under the action of the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ on the root set, coincides with the stabilizer of $\alpha$ viewed as an element of $M$ under the action of $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ on $M$. In other words, the subgroup of automorphisms in $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ fixing $\alpha$ is the same whether one regards $\alpha$ as a root point or as a field element.

description: **Inverse of the tangent adjoint map.** Let $G$ be a Lie group (modeled on a complete normed real vector space $E$ via a model with corners $I$ on a space $H$, with the Lie group structure of class $C^3$), and let $g \in G$. The tangent adjoint automorphism $\operatorname{Ad}_g$ at $g$ is a bijective map on the tangent space at the identity, and the tangent adjoint automorphism at the inverse $g^{-1}$ is exactly the inverse of the one at $g$. docstring:
A global collar of `f` is an open embedding of the boundary times `[0,1)` whose zero slice is
`f`.  The parameter is a subtype, so the endpoint `1` is excluded by construction.
description: **Global collar.** Let $M$ and $N$ be topological spaces, let $f\colon N\to M$ be a map, and let $g\colon N\times[0,1)\to M$ be a map defined on $N$ times the half-open interval $[0,1)$. The pair $(f,g)$ forms a global collar when $g$ is an open embedding, meaning it is a homeomorphism onto an open subset of $M$, and its zero slice is $f$, i.e. $g(x,0)=f(x)$ for every $x\in N$. The endpoint $1$ is excluded from the interval by construction.

**The finite-endpoint extension criterion at the left endpoint**, sequential form. If
`u n → a`, the sequence is eventually above `a`, and `γ (u n) → y`, then `γ` extends before `a`.
description: **Extension of an integral curve at a finite left endpoint (sequential criterion).** Let $M$ be a boundaryless $C^1$ (or higher) manifold modelled on a complete normed space $E$ with a Hausdorff topology, and let $v$ be a $C^1$ vector field on $M$ (a section of the tangent bundle, assumed $C^1$ as a map into the tangent bundle). Let $(u_n)$ be a sequence of real numbers with $u_n \to a$, such that eventually $u_n > a$, and suppose $\gamma(u_n)$ converges to some point $y \in M$.   CovariantDerivative.IsLeviCivitaConnection I cov →
    ∀ (X : (x : M) → TangentSpace I x),
      (MDiffAt fun x => ⟨x, Y x⟩) x →
        (MDiffAt fun x => ⟨x, Z x⟩) x →
          ((d% fun y => inner ℝ (Y y) (Z y)) x) (X x) =
            inner ℝ ((↑cov Y x) (X x)) (Z x) + inner ℝ (Y x) ((↑cov Z x) (X x))
docstring:
Metric compatibility of a Levi-Civita connection, in the usable form
`X ⟪Y, Z⟫ = ⟪∇_X Y, Z⟫ + ⟪Y, ∇_X Z⟫`: this is
`CovariantDerivative.IsMetricCompatible.mvfderiv_inner_eq` read off the defining property
`IsLeviCivitaConnection.isMetricCompatible`.
description:
**Metric compatibility of the Levi-Civita connection.** Let $M$ be a smooth manifold modeled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, equipped with a Riemannian metric (inner products on tangent spaces varying smoothly), and let $
abla$ be a covariant derivative on the tangent bundle that is a Levi-Civita connection. Let $Y$ and $Z$ be (sufficiently smooth, at least $C^1$-type differentiable at $x$) vector fields on $M$, and let $X$ be any vector field. Then, at the point $x$, the derivative of the function $y \mapsto \langle Y(y), Z(y)angle$ in the direction $X(x)$ equals
$$X\langle Y, Zangle(x) = \langle 
abla_X Y(x), Z(x)angle + \langle Y(x), 
abla_X Z(x)angle.$$
In other words, the Levi-Civita connection is compatible with the metric: differentiating inner products of vector fields obeys the product rule with respect to covariant differentiation.

name: TauCeti.SmoothTwoForm.IsSymplectic

structure TauCeti.SmoothTwoForm.IsSymplectic : {E : Type u_1} →
  {H : Type u_2} →
    {M : Type u_3} →
      [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] →
        [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] →
          [inst_2 : TopologicalSpace H] →
            {I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H} →
              [inst_3 : TopologicalSpace M] →
                [inst_4 : ChartedSpace H M] → [inst_5 : IsManifold I (↑⊤) M] → TauCeti.SmoothTwoForm I M → Prop
docstring:
A smooth two-form is **symplectic** when it is closed and fiberwise nondegenerate. This is the
manifold-level notion of a symplectic form; a symplectic manifold is a manifold carrying one.
description: **Symplectic two-form.** Let $M$ be a smooth manifold modeled on a normed space $E$ (via a model with corners $I$ on $H$), and let $\omega$ be a smooth two-form on $M$. The property of $\omega$ being symplectic means that $\omega$ is closed (its exterior derivative vanishes) and is fiberwise nondegenerate (at each point $p \in M$, the alternating bilinear form $\omega_p$ on the tangent space $T_pM$ has trivial radical, so that $\omega_p(v,w)=0$ for all $w$ forces $v=0$). This is a predicate on smooth two-forms on $M$, and a symplectic manifold is one that admits such a form.

name: TauCeti.Toric.Fan.faceAffineToricSchemeMap_comp_affineToricChartι_assoc
docstring:
The inclusion of the chart of a face factors through the face morphism into the chart of the
ambient cone.
description: **Compatibility of face inclusions with affine toric charts.** Let $N$ and $V$ be real vector spaces-type data as in the toric setup, with $\Phi$ a regular fan in $V$ (with respect to the map $i : N \to V$). Let $\tau$ and $\sigma$ be cones of $\Phi$ such that $\tau$ is a face of $\sigma$, and let $Z$ be a scheme equipped with a morphism $h_1$ from the algebraic realization of $\Phi$ to $Z$. Then, composing the morphism from the affine toric chart of $\tau$ into the affine toric chart of $\sigma$ (induced by the face inclusion) with the inclusion of the chart of $\sigma$ into the realization and with $h_1$, gives the same morphism as composing the inclusion of the chart of $\tau$ into the realization with $h_1$. In other words, the chart inclusion for a face factors through the face morphism into the chart of the ambient cone.

The free presentation of the character lattice dual to an integral basis `B` of `N`: an
integral character corresponds to the family of its values on the basis vectors.
description: **Integral Character Representation via a Basis.** Let $N$ be an abelian group and let $B = \{e_i\}_{i \in \iota}$ be a finite $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of $N$. Then there is a canonical additive group isomorphism between the group of integral characters of $N$ (the homomorphisms $N \to \mathbb{Z}$) and the free abelian group on $\iota$, finitely supported functions $\iota \to \mathbb{Z}$. The isomorphism sends a character $\chi$ to the family of its values $(\chi(e_i))_{i \in \iota}$ on the basis vectors, which is finitely supported since $\iota$ is finite.

theorem TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition.IsRecutOfRightEqRight.recut_branch : ∀ {n : ℕ} {x z : TauCeti.GridState n} {D E : TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition x z},
  D.IsRecutOfRightEqRight E →
    D.first.left ∈ TauCeti.Grid.cIoo D.second.left D.first.right ∧
        E.middle = TauCeti.GridState.swapColumns D.second.left D.first.left x ∧
          E.first.right = D.first.left ∧ E.second.right = D.first.right ∨
      D.second.left ∈ TauCeti.Grid.cIoo D.first.left D.first.right ∧
        E.middle = TauCeti.GridState.swapColumns D.second.left D.first.right x ∧
          E.first.right = D.first.right ∧ E.second.right = D.second.left
docstring: The column and branch data of a `right = right` recut.
description:
**Branch data of a right–right recut.** Let $x$ and $z$ be grid states with $n$ columns, and let $D$ and $E$ be two grid rectangle decompositions from $x$ to $z$, where $E$ is a recut of $D$ of the right-equals-right type. Write $a$ for the left column of the first rectangle of $D$, $b$ for its right column, and $c$ for the left column of the second rectangle of $D$. Then exactly one of the following two cases holds:

1. $a$ lies strictly between $c$ and $b$ (in the open interval $(c, b)$), the middle state of $E$ equals $x$ with columns $c$ and $a$ swapped, the right column of the first rectangle of $E$ is $a$, and the right column of the second rectangle of $E$ is $b$; or
2. $c$ lies strictly between $a$ and $b$ (in the open interval $(a, b)$), the middle state of $E$ equals $x$ with columns $c$ and $b$ swapped, the right column of the first rectangle of $E$ is $b$, and the right column of the second rectangle of $E$ is $c$.

name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.mem_coveredSquares_swap_iff_of_coveredColumns
signature:
theorem TauCeti.GridRectangle.mem_coveredSquares_swap_iff_of_coveredColumns : ∀ {n : ℕ} (R : TauCeti.GridRectangle n) {a b : Fin n},
  (a ∈ R.coveredColumns ↔ b ∈ R.coveredColumns) →
    ∀ (p : Fin n × Fin n), ((Equiv.swap a b) p.1, p.2) ∈ R.coveredSquares ↔ p ∈ R.coveredSquares
docstring:
Swapping two columns preserves a rectangle's covered squares when the rectangle either
covers both columns or covers neither.
description: **Swapping columns preserves covered squares when both or neither are covered.** Let $n$ be a natural number, let $R$ be a grid rectangle on an $n \times n$ grid, and let $a, b$ be two column indices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Suppose that column $a$ is covered by $R$ if and only if column $b$ is covered by $R$. Then for every square $(i, j)$ of the grid, the square obtained by applying the transposition $(a\ b)$ to its column-coordinate $i$ — that is, the square $(\sigma(i), j)$ where $\sigma$ swaps $a$ and $b$ and fixes all other indices — lies in the set of squares covered by $R$ exactly when $(i, j)$ itself does.

name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_X
signature: theorem TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_X : TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo.X = TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoSwap
docstring: The `X`-marking state of the standard two-by-two diagram is the transposition state.
description: **Marking of the standard two-by-two diagram.** The $X$-marking of the standard two-by-two grid diagram equals the transposition grid state (the state obtained by swapping the two entries).

name: TauCeti.FramedMarkovBraid
signature: structure TauCeti.FramedMarkovBraid : Type
docstring:
A framed oriented braid-closure presentation. The braid direction supplies the orientation.
A framing of an oriented link in `S³`, relative to the Seifert framing, is specified by one
integer coefficient on each component; the components of a braid closure are the orbits of its
underlying permutation. The projection `forgetFraming` drops this data to the ordinary unframed
braid on which `TauCeti.MarkovEquiv` is defined.
description: **Framed Markov braid.** A framed braid presentation of an oriented link in $S^3$: a braid together with an integer framing coefficient attached to each component of its closure, where the components correspond to the orbits of the braid's underlying permutation. The braid's direction fixes the orientation of the link. The framing is measured relative to the Seifert framing, so each component carries one integer. Forgetting these framing integers yields the ordinary unframed braid, on which the Markov equivalence relation is defined.

name: Module.Basis.coord_map_apply
signature:
theorem Module.Basis.coord_map_apply : ∀ {R : Type u_4} {M : Type u_5} {M' : Type u_6} {ι : Type u_7} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : Module R M] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M'] [inst_4 : Module R M'] (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (f : M ≃ₗ[R] M')
  (i : ι) (x : M'), ((b.map f).coord i) x = (b.coord i) (f.symm x)
docstring:
The coordinates with respect to the basis `b.map f` transported along a linear equivalence
`f` are the coordinates with respect to `b` of the vector transported back along `f`. Not a simp
lemma: simp already unfolds the left side through `Module.Basis.coord_apply`.
description: **Coordinates under a transported basis.** Let $R$ be a semiring, let $M$ and $M'$ be $R$-modules, and let $\{b_i\}_{i\in\iota}$ be a basis of $M$. Given a linear isomorphism $f\colon M \to M'$, the image family $\{f(b_i)\}_{i\in\iota}$ is a basis of $M'$, and for every index $i \in \iota$ and every vector $x \in M'$, the $i$-th coordinate of $x$ with respect to this transported basis equals the $i$-th coordinate of $f^{-1}(x)$ with respect to the original basis $b$. In other words, taking coordinates in the transported basis is the same as first pulling the vector back along $f$ and then taking its coordinates in $b$.

name: TauCeti.torusCharacter_sub
signature:
theorem TauCeti.torusCharacter_sub : ∀ {κ : Type v} {R : Type w} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Fintype κ] (s : κ → Rˣ) (μ ν : κ → ℤ),
  TauCeti.torusCharacter s (μ - ν) = TauCeti.torusCharacter s μ / TauCeti.torusCharacter s ν
docstring: Subtracting weights divides the values of their characters.
description:
**Torus characters turn differences of weights into quotients.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\kappa$ a finite index set, and $s = (s_i)_{i\in\kappa}$ a family of units of $R$. For integer weight vectors $\mu, 
u \in \mathbb{Z}^\kappa$, the character of $s$ at the difference $\mu - 
u$ equals the character at $\mu$ divided by the character at $
u$. Here the character at a weight $\mu$ is the product $\prod_{i\in\kappa} s_i^{\mu_i}$, so the identity reads $\prod_i s_i^{\mu_i - 
u_i} =  ig(\prod_i s_i^{\mu_i} ig) ig(\prod_i s_i^{
u_i} ig)^{-1}$.

name: TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv_ι
signature:
theorem TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv_ι : ∀ (p q : ℕ) (v : Fin (p + 1 + (q + 1)) → ℝ),
  (TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv p q) ((CliffordAlgebra.ι (TauCeti.realCliffordForm (p + 1) (q + 1))) v) =
    (CliffordAlgebra.ι (TauCeti.realCliffordForm p q)) ((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ] !![0, 1; 1, 0] +
      1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
        !![((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 0, ((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 1;
          -((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 1, -((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 0]
docstring:
`realCliffordBottEquiv` first separates the last positive and negative coordinates, then
applies the hyperbolic-plane equivalence.
description:
**Bott Equivalence on Generators.** For natural numbers $p, q$ and any vector $v$ in $\mathbb{R}^{(p+1)+(q+1)}$, equipped with the quadratic form of signature $(p+1, q+1)$, the Bott equivalence $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{p+1,q+1}) \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{p,q}) \otimes \mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{1,1})$ sends the image of $v$ under the canonical generator map to the following element. Let $(w, (a, b))$ be the components of the split isometry applied to $v$, where $w$ is a vector in the $(p,q)$-part and $(a,b)$ is a pair of reals. Then the image equals

$$\iota(w) \otimes \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \;+\; 1 \otimes \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ -b & -a \end{pmatrix},$$

where $\iota(w)$ is the canonical generator image of $w$ in $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{p,q})$. In words, the equivalence first splits off the last positive and negative coordinates of $v$ (via the split isometry), and then applies the hyperbolic-plane equivalence, so that the generator $v$ is mapped to the stated sum of tensors.

name: TauCeti.realCliffordZeroOneIsometry_apply
signature: theorem TauCeti.realCliffordZeroOneIsometry_apply : ∀ (v : Fin (0 + 1) → ℝ), TauCeti.realCliffordZeroOneIsometry v = v 0
docstring: `realCliffordZeroOneIsometry` reads off the single coordinate.
description: **Evaluation of the real Clifford zero-one isometry.** For every vector $v$ in $\mathbb{R}^{1}$ (that is, a function from the one-element index set $\{0\}$ to $\mathbb{R}$), applying the map $\text{realCliffordZeroOneIsometry}$ to $v$ returns the single coordinate $v_0$ of $v$.

name: QuadraticMap.IsometryEquiv.spinGroupEquiv_apply
docstring: The equivalence induced on Spin groups agrees with the forward isometry map.
description: **Spin group equivalence agrees with the induced map.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be $R$-modules, and let $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ be quadratic forms on $M_1$ and $M_2$ respectively. Suppose $e$ is an isometry equivalence between $(M_1, Q_1)$ and $(M_2, Q_2)$. Then for every element $x$ of the spin group of $Q_1$, applying the spin-group equivalence induced by $e$ to $x$ gives the same result as applying the spin-group map induced by the underlying forward isometry of $e$ to $x$.

name: TauCeti.FiniteBilinearModule.quotientOfLeRadicalMk_apply
signature:
theorem TauCeti.FiniteBilinearModule.quotientOfLeRadicalMk_apply : ∀ (A : TauCeti.FiniteBilinearModule) (K : AddSubgroup A.carrier) (hK : K ≤ A.radical) (x : A.carrier),
  (A.quotientOfLeRadicalMk K hK) x = Submodule.Quotient.mk x
docstring: The quotient map sends an element to its quotient class.
description: **Quotient Map Evaluation.** Let $A$ be a finite bilinear module, let $K$ be an additive subgroup of the carrier of $A$ contained in the radical of $A$, and let $x$ be an element of the carrier of $A$. Then the induced quotient map from $A$ by $K$ (defined using the inclusion $K \le \operatorname{rad}(A)$) sends $x$ to its equivalence class $x + (\text{radical part})$ in the quotient, i.e. the class of $x$ under the canonical quotient projection.

name: TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.zmodStandard_quadratic
signature:
theorem TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.zmodStandard_quadratic : ∀ (m : ℕ) [inst : NeZero m] (hm : Even m) (x : ZMod m),
  (TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.zmodStandard m hm).quadratic x = (TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.zmodStandardMap m hm) x
docstring: The quadratic map of the standard quadratic module is `x ↦ x² / (2m)`.
description: **Quadratic form of the standard quadratic module.** For every positive integer $m$ that is even and every element $x \in \mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$, the quadratic map of the standard finite quadratic module on $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ evaluated at $x$ agrees with the standard map defined on $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$, which sends $x$ to $x^2/(2m)$ (interpreted as a value in $\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$ via lifting $x$ to an integer representative).

name: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.orthogonalSumFst_apply
signature:
theorem TauCeti.IntegralLattice.orthogonalSumFst_apply : ∀ {V : Type u} {W : Type v} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : Module ℚ V] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup W]
  [inst_3 : Module ℚ W] (L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V) (M : TauCeti.IntegralLattice W)
  (p : ↥(L.orthogonalSum M).carrier), (L.orthogonalSumFst M) p = ((L.orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv M) p).1
description: **Projection onto the first factor of an orthogonal sum.** Let $V$ and $W$ be rational vector spaces, and let $L$ and $M$ be integral lattices in $V$ and $W$ respectively. Their orthogonal sum has a carrier set consisting of pairs of elements, and there is a canonical identification of this carrier with a product of the form (element of $L$-side, element of $M$-side). The statement asserts that for every element $p$ of the carrier of the orthogonal sum, applying the first-factor projection map $L.\mathrm{orthogonalSumFst}\ M$ to $p$ gives the same result as first transporting $p$ through the canonical carrier equivalence $L.\mathrm{orthogonalSumCarrierEquiv}\ M$ and then taking the first component of the resulting pair.

name: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeARootLattice
signature: def TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeARootLattice : (n : ℕ) → TauCeti.IntegralLattice (Fin n → ℚ)
docstring:
The positive root lattice of type `Aₙ`: the rank-`n` integral lattice on `Fin n → ℚ` whose
Gram matrix in the standard basis of simple roots is `CartanMatrix.A n`.
description: **Root lattice of type $A_n$.** For each natural number $n$, this defines an integral lattice of rank $n$ living in the rational vector space $\mathbb{Q}^n$ (vectors indexed by $\{1,\dots,n\}$). Its inner product is specified so that, in the standard basis of simple roots, the Gram matrix is the Cartan matrix of type $A_n$, i.e. the tridiagonal matrix with entries $2$ on the diagonal, $-1$ on the immediate off-diagonals, and $0$ elsewhere.

name: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isPosSemidef_iff
signature:
theorem TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isPosSemidef_iff : ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : Module ℚ V] (L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V),
  L.IsPosSemidef ↔ ∀ (x : V), 0 ≤ (L.form x) x
docstring: Positive-semidefiniteness has its usual elementwise characterization.
description: **Positive semidefiniteness of an integral lattice.** For any rational vector space $V$ equipped with an integral lattice $L$ and its associated bilinear form, $L$ is positive semidefinite if and only if the quadratic value $B(x,x)$ is nonnegative for every vector $x \in V$.

name: TauCeti.GL2Borel.quotientEquivOnePoint_symm_infty
signature:
theorem TauCeti.GL2Borel.quotientEquivOnePoint_symm_infty : ∀ (F : Type u) [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : DecidableEq F],
  (TauCeti.GL2Borel.quotientEquivOnePoint F).symm OnePoint.infty = ↑1
docstring: The coset carried to `∞` is the Borel subgroup itself.
description: **Coset of the Borel at infinity.** For every field $F$ (with decidable equality), the inverse of the canonical bijection between the coset space $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)/B(F)$, where $B(F)$ is the Borel subgroup of upper triangular matrices, and the projective line $\mathbb{P}^1(F) = F \cup \{\infty\}$ sends the point $\infty$ to the coset of the identity matrix, that is, to the Borel subgroup itself.

name: TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex
signature: inductive TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex : ℕ → Type
docstring:
An extensional index for the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group.

Difference roots retain their ordered pair of indices. The symmetric positive- and negative-sum
roots store their indices in increasing order, so each root has only one index.
description: **Indices for root subgroups of the symplectic group.** For each natural number $n$, this defines a type of indices labelling the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group of rank $n$. Difference roots are indexed by ordered pairs of indices, so the order matters. The positive-sum and negative-sum roots are indexed by unordered pairs, represented by storing the two indices in increasing order, so each such root corresponds to exactly one index.

name: Matrix.pairMinor_transpose
signature:
theorem Matrix.pairMinor_transpose : ∀ {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] (g : Matrix m n R) (p : m × m) (q : n × n),
  g.transpose.pairMinor q p = g.pairMinor p q
docstring:
A minor of the transpose is the minor of the matrix with the row and column pairs
exchanged.
description: **Transpose of a pair minor.** Let $g$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over a commutative ring $R$, let $p = (p_1, p_2)$ be a pair of row indices from $m$, and let $q = (q_1, q_2)$ be a pair of column indices from $n$. Taking the pair minor of the transpose $g^{T}$ with row pair $q$ and column pair $p$ gives the same result as taking the pair minor of $g$ with row pair $p$ and column pair $q$. In other words, transposing a matrix simply exchanges the roles of the row and column pairs in forming a pair minor.

name: TauCeti.SL2Borel.coe_mk
signature: theorem TauCeti.SL2Borel.coe_mk : ∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] (a : Rˣ) (b : R), ↑↑(TauCeti.SL2Borel.mk a b) = !![↑a, b; 0, ↑a⁻¹]
docstring: The matrix underlying `mk a b`.
description: **Matrix of the Borel element $(a, b)$.** For any commutative ring $R$, any unit $a \in R^\times$, and any element $b \in R$, the element of the $\mathrm{SL}_2$ Borel subgroup built from the pair $(a, b)$ has underlying $2 \times 2$ matrix equal to the upper triangular matrix with diagonal entries $a$ and $a^{-1}$, upper-right entry $b$, and lower-left entry $0$, i.e. $\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & a^{-1} \end{pmatrix}$.

name: TauCeti.RegularFormPresentation.one_apply
signature:
theorem TauCeti.RegularFormPresentation.one_apply : ∀ {K : Type u} [inst : Field K] (i : Fin TauCeti.RegularFormPresentation.one.fst),
  TauCeti.RegularFormPresentation.one.snd i = 1
docstring: The sole weight of the unit presentation is one.
description: **Unit Presentation Weights.** For every field $K$ and every index $i$ in the index set of the unit regular form presentation, the weight assigned to $i$ is $1$. In other words, the unit presentation has weight $1$ at each of its indices, so its sole weight is one.

name: TauCeti.mem_closure_image_piAlgebraMap
signature:
theorem TauCeti.mem_closure_image_piAlgebraMap : ∀ {κ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} (S : Type u_3) [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  {ι : Type u_4} {g : ι → κ → R} {s : Set ι} {x : κ → R},
  x ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure (g '' s) →
    (Pi.algebraMap κ R S) x ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure ((fun i => (Pi.algebraMap κ R S) (g i)) '' s)
docstring:
Entrywise base change carries the additive closure of a family into the additive closure of the
base-changed family.
description:
**Entrywise base change preserves additive closure membership.** Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with $S$ an $R$-algebra, let $\kappa$ and $\iota$ be arbitrary index types, let $\{g_i\}_{i\in\iota}$ be a family of vectors $g_i \in R^\kappa$, and let $s \subseteq \iota$. If a vector $x \in R^\kappa$ lies in the additive submonoid generated by the set $\{g_i : i \in s\}$, then the image $\varphi(x)$ of $x$ under the coordinatewise map $\varphi: R^\kappa \to S^\kappa$ induced by the structure map $R \to S$ lies in the additive submonoid of $S^\kappa$ generated by $\{\varphi(g_i) : i \in s\}$.

In other words, applying the ring map entrywise sends sums of (nonnegative integer) combinations of the vectors $g_i$, $i \in s$, to sums of the corresponding combinations of the base-changed vectors $\varphi(g_i)$.

name: TauCeti.DynkinType.TypeB.abs_rootOfPair_dotProduct_corootOfPair_le_two
signature:
theorem TauCeti.DynkinType.TypeB.abs_rootOfPair_dotProduct_corootOfPair_le_two : ∀ {n : ℕ} {u v p q : Fin (2 * n)},
  TauCeti.DynkinType.TypeB.IsPair u v →
    TauCeti.DynkinType.TypeB.IsPair p q →
      |TauCeti.DynkinType.TypeB.rootOfPair u v ⬝ᵥ TauCeti.DynkinType.TypeB.corootOfPair p q| ≤ 2
docstring:
Cartan integers between roots in the classical type `B` model have absolute value at most
two.
description: **Cartan Integers Bounded by Two in Type B.** For every natural number $n$ and any indices $u, v, p, q$ in $\{0, 1, \ldots, 2n-1\}$ such that $(u,v)$ is a pair and $(p,q)$ is a pair (in the sense of the classical type $B$ model), the absolute value of the dot product of the root associated with $(u,v)$ with the coroot associated with $(p,q)$ is at most $2$. In other words, $|\langle \alpha_{uv}, \alpha^\vee_{pq}\rangle| \le 2$ for all such pairs.

name: TauCeti.mem_weylChamber
signature:
theorem TauCeti.mem_weylChamber : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} {M : Type u_3} {N : Type u_4} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup M]
  [inst_2 : Module R M] [inst_3 : AddCommGroup N] [inst_4 : Module R N] (P : RootPairing ι R M N)
  [inst_5 : LinearOrder R] (b : P.Base) (w : ↥P.weylGroup) (x : M),
  x ∈ TauCeti.weylChamber P b w ↔ w⁻¹ • x ∈ TauCeti.dominantChamber P b
docstring: Membership in a closed Weyl chamber, pulled back to the dominant one.
description: **Membership in a closed Weyl chamber.** Let $P$ be a root pairing with indices in $\iota$, over a linear-ordered commutative ring $R$, with weight space $M$ and coroot space $N$, and let $b$ be a base of $P$. For an element $w$ of the Weyl group of $P$ and a vector $x \in M$, the vector $x$ lies in the closed Weyl chamber associated with $w$ if and only if $w^{-1}$ applied to $x$ lies in the closed dominant chamber determined by $b$. In other words, pulling $x$ back by $w^{-1}$ moves the question to the dominant chamber.

name: TauCeti.SymmetricAlgebra.map_homogeneousSubmodule_equivMvPolynomial
signature:
theorem TauCeti.SymmetricAlgebra.map_homogeneousSubmodule_equivMvPolynomial : ∀ (R : Type u) (M : Type v) [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M] {ι : Type w}
  (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (n : ℕ),
  Submodule.map (SymmetricAlgebra.equivMvPolynomial b).toLinearMap
      (TauCeti.SymmetricAlgebra.homogeneousSubmodule R M n) =
    MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule ι R n
docstring: The algebra equivalence induced by a basis preserves homogeneous degree.
description: **Symmetric algebra degree-preservation under a basis.** Let $R$ be a commutative semiring, $M$ an $R$-module, and $b$ an $R$-basis of $M$ indexed by a type $\iota$. Let $\operatorname{Sym}(M)$ denote the symmetric algebra of $M$, and let $\operatorname{Sym}_n(M)$ be its homogeneous submodule of degree $n$. The algebra isomorphism $\operatorname{Sym}(M) \cong R[\iota]$ (polynomials in variables indexed by $\iota$) induced by the basis $b$ sends the degree-$n$ homogeneous part of $\operatorname{Sym}(M)$ exactly onto the degree-$n$ homogeneous polynomials in $R[\iota]$. In other words, the image of $\operatorname{Sym}_n(M)$ under this isomorphism equals the submodule of homogeneous polynomials of degree $n$ in the variables indexed by $\iota$ with coefficients in $R$.

name: TauCeti.HeegaardIntersectionSystem
signature: structure TauCeti.HeegaardIntersectionSystem : ℕ → Type u → Type u
docstring:
Finite intersection data for two equally sized curve systems. The finite enumeration records
the point set, and each point has one `α`-curve label and one `β`-curve label; geometric surface
and region data are additional structure.
description: **Heegaard Intersection System.** For a natural number $g$ and a type $\alpha$ of points, a Heegaard intersection system of genus $g$ consists of finite intersection data for two families of $g$ curves, one family labelled by $\alpha$-curves and the other by $\beta$-curves. Concretely, it is a finite set of intersection points together with, for each point, a label identifying one $\alpha$-curve and one $\beta$-curve passing through it. The structure records only this combinatorial incidence data; any geometric information about the underlying surface or the regions it cuts out is extra structure carried alongside, not part of this basic data.

name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_nondegenerate
signature:
theorem TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_nondegenerate : ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] [inst_1 : Fintype V] {P : TauCeti.PlumbingGraph V},
  P.IsNegativeDefinite → P.intersectionForm.Nondegenerate
docstring:
The intersection form of a negative-definite plumbing is nondegenerate: a lattice vector that
pairs to zero with every vector — in particular with itself — is zero, on either side.
description: **Nondegeneracy of the intersection form of a negative-definite plumbing.** For any finite plumbing graph $P$ on a finite vertex set $V$, if $P$ is negative definite, then its intersection form is nondegenerate: whenever a lattice vector $x$ satisfies $\langle x, y\rangle = 0$ for every vector $y$ (in particular, when $\langle x, x\rangle = 0$), we must have $x = 0$, and the same holds with the roles of the two arguments exchanged.

name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_blowUpCharacteristic_eq_iff
signature:
theorem TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicWeight_blowUpCharacteristic_eq_iff : ∀ {V : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq V] (P : TauCeti.PlumbingGraph V) (v : V) [inst_1 : Fintype V]
  (k : P.characteristicVectors) (ε : ℤ) (hε : Odd ε) (x : V → ℤ) (s : ℤ),
  (P.blowUpVertex v).characteristicWeight (P.blowUpCharacteristic v k ε hε)
        ((TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.blowUpVertexEquiv v) (x, s)) =
      P.characteristicWeight k x ↔
    s = 0 ∨ s = ε
docstring:
The blown-up weight agrees with the old weight exactly at the two exceptional multiplicities
`0` and `ε`, the two lattice points of the exceptional direction where the term `s * (s - ε)`
vanishes.
description: **Blow-up weight agrees with the original weight exactly at the two exceptional multiplicities.** Let $P$ be a plumbing graph on a finite vertex set with a chosen vertex $v$, let $k$ be a characteristic vector of $P$, and let $\varepsilon$ be an odd integer with associated blown-up characteristic $\mathrm{blowUpCharacteristic}(v,k,\varepsilon)$ on the blown-up graph $P$ blown up at $v$. Given an integer assignment $x$ on the original vertices and an integer $s$ (the multiplicity at the new exceptional vertex), identify the pair $(x,s)$ with a vertex-labelling of the blown-up graph via the blow-up equivalence. Then the characteristic weight of the blown-up graph at this labelling equals the characteristic weight of $P$ at $k$ and $x$ if and only if $s = 0$ or $s = \varepsilon$. In other words, the two weights coincide precisely at the two lattice points $s=0$ and $s=\varepsilon$ of the exceptional direction, where the extra correction term $s(s-\varepsilon)$ vanishes.

name: TauCeti.enorm_setAverage_rpow_le
signature:
theorem TauCeti.enorm_setAverage_rpow_le : ∀ {α : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ F] {f : α → F} {s : Set α} {q : ℝ},
  1 ≤ q →
    MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f mu →
      mu s ≠ 0 → mu s ≠ ⊤ → ‖⨍ (y : α) in s, f y ∂mu‖ₑ ^ q ≤ (mu s)⁻¹ * ∫⁻ (y : α) in s, ‖f y‖ₑ ^ q ∂mu
docstring:
**Hölder's bound on an average**, in `∫⁻` form: the `q`-th power of the average of `f` over a
set `s` of finite positive measure is at most `(μ s)⁻¹` times the integral of `‖f‖ ^ q` over `s`.
The single factor `(μ s)⁻¹` is what survives after the `q`-th power of the normalization
`(μ s)⁻¹` cancels against the `(μ s) ^ (q - 1)` of Hölder's inequality.
description:
**Hölder-type bound on the average of a function over a set.** Let $(\alpha, \mu)$ be a measure space, let $F$ be a normed real vector space, and let $f : \alpha \to F$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to $\mu$. Let $s \subseteq \alpha$ be a measurable set with $0 < \mu(s) < \infty$, and let $q \ge 1$ be a real number. Then the $q$-th power of the (extended) norm of the average of $f$ over $s$ is bounded by the average of the $q$-th power of the norm:

$$\Big\|\frac{1}{\mu(s)}\int_s f\,d\mu\Big\|^{q} \;\le\; \frac{1}{\mu(s)}\int_s \|f(y)\|^{q}\,d\mu(y),$$

where the integral on the right is a lower (extended nonnegative) Lebesgue integral, so the inequality holds in $[0,\infty]$ without any integrability assumption on $f$.

name: TauCeti.symmetricMatrixSecondCountableTopology
signature: instance TauCeti.symmetricMatrixSecondCountableTopology : ∀ (p : ℕ), SecondCountableTopology ↥(selfAdjoint.submodule ℝ (Matrix (Fin p) (Fin p) ℝ))
description: **Second countability of symmetric matrices.** For every natural number $p$, the space of real self-adjoint (that is, symmetric) $p \times p$ matrices, viewed as a topological subspace of the space of all real $p \times p$ matrices, is second countable.

name: TauCeti.WassersteinSpace.pseudoEMetricSpace
signature:
def TauCeti.WassersteinSpace.pseudoEMetricSpace : {X : Type u} →
  {p : ENNReal} →
    [inst : MeasurableSpace X] →
      [inst_1 : PseudoMetricSpace X] →
        [StandardBorelSpace X] →
          (Measurable fun z => edist z.1 z.2) → 1 ≤ p → PseudoEMetricSpace (TauCeti.WassersteinSpace p X)
docstring:
The Wasserstein extended distance equips finite-moment laws with a pseudoemetric space
structure whenever the ground distance is measurable and `1 ≤ p`.
description: **Wasserstein Space Pseudo-Extended-Metric Structure.** Let $X$ be a standard Borel space equipped with a pseudometric $d$ such that the distance function $(x,y)\mapsto d(x,y)$ is measurable, and let $p \ge 1$ be an extended nonnegative real exponent. Then the space of probability laws on $X$ with finite $p$-th moment, equipped with the $p$-Wasserstein extended distance, carries the structure of a pseudo-extended-metric space. In other words, the Wasserstein extended distance is a well-defined extended pseudometric on this space of finite-moment laws (it is symmetric, satisfies the triangle inequality, and assigns zero distance to a law from itself, while allowing distinct laws to be at distance zero), and this structure is given by the hypotheses above.

name: TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative
signature: structure TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative : {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction K → Prop
docstring:
An ideal arithmetic function is multiplicative when it takes the unit ideal to `1` and
respects products of relatively prime nonzero ideals. This is weaker than the complete
multiplicativity carried by `MultiplicativeIdealWeight`.
description: **Multiplicativity of an ideal arithmetic function.** Let $K$ be a field (in the setting of ideals of a Dedekind-type ring of integers of $K$), and let $f$ be an ideal arithmetic function, i.e. a function assigning a value to each nonzero ideal. We say $f$ is multiplicative if it satisfies two conditions: first, $f$ takes the unit ideal (the whole ring) to the number $1$; second, $f$ respects products of relatively prime nonzero ideals, meaning that whenever $I$ and $J$ are nonzero ideals with no common prime factors (so that $I + J$ is the whole ring), $f(IJ) = f(I)\,f(J)$. This is strictly weaker than complete multiplicativity, which would require $f(IJ) = f(I)f(J)$ for all nonzero ideals $I$ and $J$, not just coprime ones.

name: TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerronKernel
signature:
theorem TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerronKernel : ∀ {x c : ℝ},

docstring:
As the height tends to infinity the truncated Perron kernel tends to the sharp step, at every
positive `x`; at the endpoint `x = 1` this is the half-weight limit
`TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerronKernel_one`.
description: **Limit of the truncated Perron kernel.** For every real numbers $x > 0$ and $c > 0$, the truncated Perron kernel $T(x, c)$ tends to the sharp step function value $\operatorname{perronStep}(x)$ as the height $c$ goes to infinity. In other words, $\lim_{c \to \infty} T(x, c) = \operatorname{perronStep}(x)$ for each fixed positive $x$.

name: TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder
signature:
structure TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder : (K : Type u_2) →
  [inst : Field K] →
    [NumberField K] → Set (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) → ℝ → Type
docstring:
**Boundary data for the prime Dirichlet series of `S`.**  The function `series` is the sum
of the Dirichlet series of `primeVonMangoldtCoeff K S` on `Re s > 1`.  The function `remainder`
is continuous on `Re s ≥ 1` and agrees on the open half-plane with
`series s - δ / (s - 1)`.

The functions have precisely their mathematically relevant domains, so the structure carries no
arbitrary values elsewhere.
description:
**Boundary data for the prime Dirichlet series attached to a set of primes.** Fix a number field $K$, a set $S$ of height-one (nonzero prime) ideals of its ring of integers, and a real number $\delta$. The type of boundary data consists of two complex-valued functions:

- a function $F(s)$ defined on the open half-plane $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, which is the Dirichlet series $\sum_n \Lambda_S(n)\,n^{-s}$ of the prime von Mangoldt coefficients of $S$ (taken with respect to $K$), and
- a function $R(s)$ defined on the closed half-plane $\operatorname{Re} s \ge 1$, which is continuous there and satisfies $R(s) = F(s) - \dfrac{\delta}{s-1}$ for every $s$ with $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$.

The data is thus a continuous extension to the closed half-plane of $F(s) - \delta/(s-1)$, and the two functions are defined exactly on these half-planes, with no extra values assigned elsewhere.

name: TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight.map

def TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight.map : {K : Type u_1} →

    [inst_1 : NumberField K] →
      {L : Type u_2} →
        [inst_2 : Field L] →
          [inst_3 : NumberField L] → K ≃+* L → TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight K → TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight L
docstring:
**Transport along an isomorphism of fields.** An isomorphism `e : K ≃+* L` carries a
multiplicative ideal weight on `K` to one on `L`, by pulling ideals of `𝓞 L` back to `𝓞 K`
along `NumberField.RingOfIntegers.mapRingEquiv e`.
description: **Transport of a multiplicative ideal weight along a field isomorphism.** Let $K$ and $L$ be number fields, and let $e : K \to L$ be a field isomorphism. This induces a ring isomorphism between their rings of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ and $\mathcal{O}_L$. Given a multiplicative ideal weight on $K$, this construction produces a multiplicative ideal weight on $L$ by transporting it along $e$: the value assigned to an ideal of $\mathcal{O}_L$ is the value the original weight assigns to the corresponding ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$.

name: NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_subset_compl_ramifiedPrimes
signature:
theorem NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet_subset_compl_ramifiedPrimes : ∀ {K : Type u_1} {L : Type u_2} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] [inst_2 : Field L] [inst_3 : NumberField L]

docstring: No ramified prime carries an Artin class: the fibres avoid `ramifiedPrimes K L`.
description: **Frobenius primes avoid ramified primes.** Let $K$ be a number field and $L$ a Galois extension of $K$ (with $L$ a number field), and let $C$ be a conjugacy class of the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$. Then the set of prime ideals of $K$ whose Artin (Frobenius) class is $C$ is disjoint from the set of primes of $K$ that ramify in $L$. In other words, every prime $\mathfrak{p}$ of $K$ that lies in the Chebotarev set associated to $C$ is unramified in $L/K$.

description: **Order of the second cohomology group of a finite normal layer.** Let $G$ be a profinite-type group (a compact, totally disconnected topological group), let $F$ be a class formation over $G$, and let $L$ be a finite normal layer of this class formation. Then the second cohomology group $H^2$ of $L$ (with respect to $F$) is finite, and its cardinality equals the degree $[K:F]$ of the layer, i.e. the index of the corresponding field extension.

name: TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.LayerRestriction.trivialTateCor
signature:
def TauCeti.ClassFieldTheory.LayerRestriction.trivialTateCor : {G : Type} →

**Corestriction on the Tate cohomology of finite normal layers with trivial integral
coefficients, in every integer degree.** It uses cohomological corestriction in positive degrees,
the low-degree norm maps in degrees zero and minus one, and homological corestriction below them.
description: **Corestriction on trivial-coefficient Tate cohomology of normal layers.** Let $G$ be a profinite-style group: a compact, totally disconnected topological group. Given two normal layers $\text{small}$ and $\text{big}$ of $G$ together with a layer restriction map between them, and given any integer $r$, there is a morphism from the degree-$r$ Tate cohomology of $\text{small}$ with trivial integral coefficients to the degree-$r$ Tate cohomology of $\text{big}$. This morphism is the corestriction map: in positive degrees it is the cohomological corestriction, in degrees zero and minus one it is the low-degree norm maps, and in degrees below minus one it is the homological corestriction.

name: Subgroup.dirichletConductor_bot

docstring: The trivial character group has conductor one.
description: **Conductor of the trivial subgroup.** For every commutative monoid with zero $R$ and every positive integer $n$, the Dirichlet conductor of the trivial subgroup (the bottom element of the subgroup lattice, containing only the identity) is $1$. In other words, the trivial group of Dirichlet characters modulo $n$ has conductor one.

docstring: The denominator of the invariant of `normEDS b c d` at `s = 1`, `n = 2`: it is `c * b`.
description: **Denominator of the invariant of the norm EDS at $s=1$, $n=2$.** For any commutative ring $R$ and any elements $b, c, d \in R$, consider the norm elliptic divisibility sequence $\mathrm{normEDS}(b,c,d)$ attached to $b, c, d$. The denominator appearing in the invariant of this sequence at the indices $s = 1$ and $n = 2$ equals $cb$, i.e. the product of $c$ and $b$.

name: IsEllipticNet.atomRel_swap₃₄

theorem IsEllipticNet.atomRel_swap₃₄ : ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {W : ℤ → R},

docstring: Transposing the last two indices negates the relator.
description: **Antisymmetry of the elliptic net atomic relator in its last two indices.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $W:\mathbb{Z}\to R$ be an odd function, meaning $W(-n) = -W(n)$ for all integers $n$. Then for all integers $a, b, c, d$, the atomic relator $\operatorname{atomRel}_W(a,b,c,d)$ satisfies $\operatorname{atomRel}_W(a,b,c,d) = -\operatorname{atomRel}_W(a,b,d,c)$. In other words, swapping the third and fourth indices changes the sign of the relator.

name: HeckeRing.GLn.CanonicalDiagonal

The positive divisibility chains of length `n`: the parameter space of the diagonal

description: **Canonical diagonal parameters.** For a natural number $n$, the canonical diagonal objects of length $n$ are the positive divisibility chains $(d_1, \dots, d_n)$ of positive integers with $d_1 \mid d_2 \mid \cdots \mid d_n$. These chains index the diagonal double cosets, serving as the parameter space for them.

description: **Identity of the Diamond Operator at 1.** For every natural number $N$ and every integer $k$, the diamond operator $\langle k \rangle$ applied to the element $1$ (of the relevant unit group modulo $N$) is the identity linear map.

name: TauCeti.ModularForm.galoisProd

docstring: The product `∏_{j < N} f(τ - j)`, used as a building block of the norm map.
description: **Partial Galois product.** For a commutative monoid $\alpha$, a natural number $N$, and a function $f$ from the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}$ to $\alpha$, this assigns to each point $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$ the product $\prod_{j=0}^{N-1} f(\tau - j)$ of the values of $f$ at the $N$ points $\tau, \tau-1, \dots, \tau-(N-1)$ obtained by translating $\tau$ by integer shifts. It serves as a building block for the norm map.

name: HeckeRing.GL2.coe_twistedHeckeSlashCuspFormCharLinearMap
signature:
theorem HeckeRing.GL2.coe_twistedHeckeSlashCuspFormCharLinearMap : ∀ {N : ℕ} (k : ℤ) (χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ) [inst : NeZero N]
  (T :
    HeckeRing (HeckeRing.GL2.Delta0 N) (Subgroup.map (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.mapGL ℚ) (CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0 N))
      ℤ)
  (f : ↥(cuspFormCharSpace k χ)),
  ⇑↑(((HeckeRing.GL2.twistedHeckeSlashCuspFormCharLinearMap k χ) T) f) =
    ↑(((HeckeRing.GL2.twistedHeckeSlashRingCharLinearMap k χ) T) ⟨⇑↑f, ⋯⟩)
docstring: On underlying functions, the cusp-form extension is the function-space extension.
description: **Compatibility of the cusp-form Hecke action with the underlying function action.** Let $N \ge 1$ be a natural number, $k$ an integer weight, and $\chi$ a group homomorphism from $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ to $\mathbb{C}^\times$ (a Dirichlet-type character mod $N$). Let $T$ be an element of the Hecke ring of the pair consisting of the double coset monoid $\Delta_0(N)$ (in $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$) and the image of $\Gamma_0(N)$, with integer coefficients. Let $f$ be a cusp form in the space $S_k(N,\chi)$ of cusp forms of weight $k$ and character $\chi$. Then the function underlying the cusp form $T\cdot f$, obtained by applying the twisted Hecke operator defined on cusp forms, coincides as a function on the upper half-plane with the function underlying the result of applying the twisted Hecke operator defined on the full space of holomorphic-type slash-invariant functions (the ring-level twisted Hecke action) to the underlying function of $f$. In other words, the cusp-form Hecke action is just the restriction of the ambient function-space Hecke action.

name: TauCeti.ModularForm.finiteDimensional_modularForm_finiteIndex

instance TauCeti.ModularForm.finiteDimensional_modularForm_finiteIndex : ∀ {𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ)} [inst : 𝒢.HasDetOne] [𝒢.IsFiniteRelIndex (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.mapGL ℝ).range]
